title: Matt LaFleur: 'He's playing like an animal right now'
headline: Golden was the offensive player of the game, Van Ness is 'playing like an animal,' and the Packers' O-line is a patchwork with Banks a game-time call for Thursday at Atlanta.
summary: LaFleur opened by saying a key offensive lineman (apparently Zach Tom, who isn't on the provided roster) is back in Green Bay for testing after re-injuring the same knee. It is too early to discuss a return this season, and the offense will have to adjust to losing him. Anthony Belton will be the right tackle if healthy, and LaFleur expects him to play. Aaron Banks is a game-time decision for Thursday. Jager Burton played 23 snaps, and LaFleur expects him to keep playing even though Banks is the starter when healthy. LaFleur praised Matthew Golden as the offensive player of the game for fixing his drop-step technique and for his lob-pass touchdown-style play with Jordan Love. He was frustrated by the offense: last in completion percentage, last in third-down distance, and 26 penalties through two games. He wants to run more consistently and have Love use his legs when the pocket opens. Kaleb Johnson's good overtime run was noted despite the fumble, Skyy Moore's returns are creating short fields, and Lukas Van Ness got strong praise with Micah Parsons expected back in a couple of weeks. Next up is Atlanta on Thursday night, and LaFleur expects a different offense with Penix at QB.

injuries.detail: Re-injured the same knee; back in Green Bay for testing and consultations. LaFleur said it is too early to say whether he returns this season.
Expected to be the right tackle if healthy. LaFleur anticipates him playing but said there are still 48 hours until the game.
Availability for Thursday will be decided up to game time.
LaFleur confirmed the injury was to his neck, not his back. The player can't be identified with confidence.

signals.claim: Golden will keep a growing target share in the passing game.
signals.note: He was named the offensive player of the game and is getting more looks than last season, making him a rising WR option.
signals.quote: he was our offensive player of the game.

signals.claim: Van Ness will continue as an impact edge defender, with availability the main concern.
signals.note: IDP managers should note his hot start, with Parsons expected to join him in a couple of weeks.
signals.quote: he's playing like an animal right now

signals.claim: Belton will start at right tackle if healthy for Thursday.
signals.note: O-line stability affects the run game and Love's pass protection.
signals.quote: He'll be the right tackle.

signals.claim: Banks's Thursday status won't be decided until game time.
signals.note: His absence would change the O-line makeup on a short week.
signals.quote: Well we'll give it up to game time.

signals.claim: Burton will play meaningful snaps along the offensive line.
signals.note: He is competing with Banks at left guard and will likely see more action given the O-line injuries.
signals.quote: I would expect him to end up having to play some football for us.

signals.claim: Johnson could get more involvement in the run game after a strong overtime opening run.
signals.note: A ball-security issue remains, but LaFleur credited his 12-yard outside-zone run with sparking the offense.
signals.quote: I think that that was big for us.

signals.claim: Moore will remain the primary returner, giving the offense better field position.
signals.note: His returns add value in return-yardage formats and set up scoring chances.
signals.quote: Puts us in position to score a lot more points.

signals.claim: Love should run more when the pocket opens, though LaFleur called it situational.
signals.note: Love is last in completion percentage, but his rushing could add a fantasy floor if he is used more as a runner.
signals.quote: I think it's all feel.

topics.detail: LaFleur said the Packers are last in third-down distance and last in completion percentage. He called it a collective issue and wants to get into more third-and-short situations without overreacting in week two.
The team has 26 penalties through two games. LaFleur called the pre-snap penalties inexcusable and chalked up two silly post-snap penalties to young players.
He praised linemen for defending Love after a hit without drawing a flag, while saying every situation is different regarding discipline.
He defended calling two handoffs to Chris Brooks in the red zone, saying the run game must be established against two-high safeties.

title: Sean McVay talks standout players in win over the Giants, competing with joy, Aaron Donald's impactful return & more
headline: Puka Nacua missed the Giants game with a groin issue and his Week 3 status is unknown, while Davante Adams took over, Blake Corum and Kyren Williams are splitting carries, and Terrance Ferguson is trusted as a versatile TE.
summary: McVay opened by saying there are no major new injuries, only bumps and bruises, with more updates coming on Puka Nacua, Cam Curl and Kamren Kinchens. Nacua practiced Thursday but felt sore in the groin, and the Rams treated him as a bonus if he played. McVay is hopeful he returns next week but does not know his status. Jordan Whittington was also out. Terrance Ferguson moved around, blocked well and scored after an earlier drop, and McVay praised his toughness and value. Davante Adams had a big night, with early involvement and contested catches and two touchdowns alongside Matthew Stafford, and McVay admitted he did not get Adams going in the opener. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum have essentially split carries, and McVay called them two great backs who spell each other. Aaron Donald returned and played 30-plus snaps, still drawing double and triple teams. On defense, Wesley Bailey got his first career sack with Myles Garrett out, and Trent McDuffie was outstanding. Tank McCollough, Josh Wallace and Cam Curl got a lot of snaps. The next game is on a short week against Jacksonville.

injuries.detail: Groin soreness, soft-tissue injury; sat out the Giants game. McVay is hopeful for next week but unsure, and will give an update.
Missed the Giants game; the Rams knew beforehand he would be out.
McVay said he would have further updates on him after the game's bumps and bruises.
Was out for the game, which opened up reps for the edge group.

signals.claim: Nacua's availability for next week's game is uncertain; the Rams will see if he is ready to go.
signals.note: His Week 3 status is unresolved, so monitor practice reports before setting lineups.

signals.claim: Adams will be involved early and often alongside Stafford.
signals.note: He dominated with contested catches and touchdowns, and McVay admitted he should have gotten him going sooner in Week 1.
signals.quote: I thought getting him involved early was key.

signals.claim: Ferguson will keep a significant, versatile role as a tight end who moves around, catches and blocks.
signals.note: He got major snaps with Nacua out and caught a touchdown, so he has streaming appeal in deeper TE formats.
signals.quote: So his value is tremendous to us.

signals.claim: Corum and Williams will continue splitting carries and spelling each other.
signals.note: The backfield looks like a split, which caps the upside for both.

signals.claim: Williams will continue sharing carries with Corum.
signals.note: A near-even split limits his workload ceiling.
signals.quote: Kyron is obviously such a stud, so valuable and in both phases

signals.claim: Bailey will keep rotating in on the edge, with Garrett out.
signals.note: He is a rotational pass rusher with a first career sack, which matters for IDP.
signals.quote: That was awesome for him to be able to get his first career sack.

signals.claim: Donald will keep playing a significant defensive line role as he gets more reps.
signals.note: He played 30-plus snaps in his return and still draws double and triple teams, which is good for IDP and the interior line.
signals.quote: still eliciting double and triple teams because of who he is.

signals.note: McVay singled him out as outstanding in a strong defensive performance.
signals.quote: Trent McDuffie was outstanding

signals.note: He had strong protection and chemistry with Adams, which helps the passing game.

topics.detail: McVay credited an attacking mindset, a consistent pass rush and sticky coverage for limiting explosive plays, with 'tank' McCollough, Josh Wallace and Cam Curl getting more snaps.
The line protected Stafford well against a talented Giants pass rush, with some protection adjustments and tight end help.
McVay said it was not a good day, citing field position and a strong opposing punter.
A short week lets the team start prepping right away, now that they have film on the first two games.

title: Coach John Harbaugh on latest with QB Jaxson Dart
headline: Jaxson Dart's injury is still under evaluation after an MRI, with reports of a possible season-ending issue unconfirmed. Harbaugh expressed 'absolute faith' in Jameis Winston as the next man up; Dart is a major risk for Week 4 vs. Tennessee.
summary: Harbaugh refused to confirm or deny reports that Jaxson Dart could miss the season, saying evaluations are ongoing and no final decisions have been made. He confirmed Dart had an MRI and that doctors are now consulting on the results, but he declined to say whether the injury is worse than the initial sprained MCL diagnosis. He called it unfair to give a running report on a player's health while conversations are happening. Asked about Jameis Winston, he voiced absolute faith in him as a very good football player and the next man up, without formally naming him the starter. He said Dart was disappointed after the loss and, he believes, was trying to get back into the game. Harbaugh also noted Deonte Banks (Tay Banks in the captions) missed the last game, and he stressed that injuries are part of the league. He played down the emotional challenge of replacing a starting QB, saying the team will prepare for a range of possibilities with Tennessee five days away. He said the team has not come close to playing up to its potential.

injuries.detail: Had an MRI; doctors are still consulting and evaluating results. Harbaugh would not confirm reports of a season-ending injury or whether it is worse than the sprained MCL initially described. Dart reportedly wanted to return to the game.
Missed the most recent game; Harbaugh called it tough but gave no further timeline.

signals.claim: A final decision on Dart's injury and availability will be announced once evaluations are complete; his status for Tennessee is unresolved.
signals.note: Dart's availability is highly uncertain and reports suggest he could miss significant time, so fantasy managers should line up a backup plan.
signals.quote: evaluations are are ongoing. We haven't got any final decisions yet.

signals.claim: Winston is the next quarterback up if Dart is unavailable.
signals.note: Winston becomes a potential starter and a streaming/QB2 option, and the passing-game pieces could shift with him under center.
signals.quote: Absolute faith in all of our players.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said the team hasn't come close to playing as well as it can, and the 'next man up' mentality applies. He emphasized preparing for a range of outcomes and winning as a complete team.
He declined to comment on media reports, saying the process involves multiple people and he won't breach trust or speak for the doctors or the player.

title: Postgame Press Conference: Coach John Harbaugh on Jaxson Dart's status
headline: Jaxson Dart is likely dealing with a sprained MCL and gets an MRI Tuesday. Brian Burns (low ankle sprain) and Andrew Thomas also got hurt, and Malik Nabers returned to the game.
summary: Harbaugh said the Giants have a lot of work to do after the Week 2 loss to the Rams and must turn the game around within six days. He called the reported sprained MCL for Jaxson Dart 'in the neighborhood' of the diagnosis. An MRI on Tuesday will give a clearer picture, and he wouldn't say whether he is bracing to be without Dart. He did say it's good news that the injury isn't the devastating outcome. Brian Burns has a low ankle sprain, and Andrew Thomas was banged up in the last four minutes with no update. Harbaugh said injured players may return this week or next. He was encouraged that Malik Nabers came back into the game. He said Jameis Winston operated the offense well in relief, but the whole team failed to execute, complete passes, run the ball or make plays downfield. He admitted the play calling, including four straight runs from the 11-yard line, will be second-guessed. He said the Rams' interior games were the biggest pass-rush problem, and the Giants got little pressure on Matthew Stafford.

injuries.detail: NFL Network reported a sprained MCL and Harbaugh said that is in the neighborhood of the diagnosis. An MRI is scheduled for Tuesday, and he said the fact it isn't the devastating outcome is good news. Dart's spirits are good.
Low ankle sprain. Harbaugh said injured players may be back this week or next.
Got banged up in the last four minutes. Harbaugh said 'we'll see about that' and gave no diagnosis.
Left the game but came back, which Harbaugh called good news. He said nothing was plaguing Nabers.
Harbaugh referenced 'Teo' getting back as soon as he can, which suggests he is currently out. The captions don't say more, and the name is likely Theo Johnson.

signals.claim: Dart's availability for the next game will be clearer after Tuesday's MRI.
signals.note: A sprained MCL could cost Dart time, and the Giants' Week 3 QB situation depends on the MRI result.
signals.quote: we'll get an MRI tomorrow and have a really good feel for it

signals.note: Winston played in relief and Harbaugh praised how he ran the offense, so he is the fallback if Dart misses time.
signals.quote: He came in executed. He operated really well.

signals.claim: Burns has a low ankle sprain and could return this week or next.
signals.note: A low ankle sprain suggests a short absence at most, but he is a risk for the next game.
signals.quote: it's a sprained ankle

signals.note: The star left tackle's late injury is unresolved, and his absence would hurt the offense and pass protection.
signals.quote: Yeah we'll see about that.

signals.claim: Nabers returned to the game after getting hurt.
signals.note: His return to the game is encouraging for his health, even though he had little impact in a poor offensive outing.
signals.quote: It made me really happy to see that

topics.detail: Harbaugh said the offense didn't complete passes, run well or make plays downfield, calling it a team-wide failure to execute rather than one player's problem. He said a full answer requires watching the tape.

After recovering a fumble at the 11-yard line, the Giants ran four straight times without scoring. Harbaugh said the staff is second-guessing the calls and called it a coaching and planning issue as well as execution.
The Giants had one sack and two QB hits on over 30 dropbacks. Harbaugh said the Rams got the ball out quickly and blocked well, and that the interior games were the main problem.
Harbaugh said the Rams did nothing special with Adams and that he simply made plays. He didn't say when the Giants put Greg Newsome II on him, only that they tried a lot of ideas.
